# **SCOPE OF THE REPORT** 

The scope of this Report includes the strategic narrative and focuses on our ongoing project sites in India, developed either directly or through our special purpose vehicles. Unless stated otherwise, information and content have been consolidated for the purpose of reporting. 

Where relevant, the report also extends its boundary to include key risks and opportunities arising from entities and stakeholders that affect our ability to create value. These entities and stakeholders may not be under our direct control or influence, but play a critical role in our value creation journey due to the nature and proximity of their impact. This report details our environmental performance across 63 active project sites, and 8 offices, including our headquarters in Mumbai, which are under our direct operational control.

Godrej was founded in 1897 by Ardeshir Godrej to help build economic independence for India. We contributed to this purpose by both innovating and actively donating a significant portion of the Group’s profits to India’s freedom movement. 

During the Spanish Flu pandemic of 1918, we pioneered the world’s first commercially made soap from vegetable oil, free of animal fat. In 1951, we crafted the ballot boxes for free India’s first general election, where every citizen, regardless of gender, had the right to vote. 

This legacy of nation-building continues to guide our actions today. As we expand our footprint, we are equally focused on driving positive impact - by integrating sustainability and inclusion into everything we do. 

Through Godrej Good & Green, we align with global goals and local community needs to enable a greener, more equitable world. And through the Godrej DEI Lab, we are building inclusive ecosystems, nurturing diverse talent, and bringing DEI-driven innovation to the fore.

# **CHAIRPERSON’S MESSAGE** 

**FY 2024–25 was a landmark year for Godrej Properties— one where we saw the rewards of focused execution, customer-centricity, and longterm thinking come together. As India continues to lead global economic growth and urban transformation, the real estate sector has played a vital role in driving opportunity, progress, and impact.** 

## **PIROJSHA GODREJ** 

Executive Chairperson 

## **Dear Shareholders,** 

I hope this message finds you and your loved ones well. 

FY 2024–25 was a landmark year for Godrej Properties—one where we saw the rewards of focused execution, customer-centricity, and long-term thinking come together. As India continues to lead global economic growth and urban transformation, the real estate sector has played a vital role in driving opportunity, progress, and impact. 

At Godrej Properties, we remain guided by our core purpose: to create spaces that enable Everyday Joys: one home, one community, one city at a time. The year gone by saw us deepen our presence across key markets, introduce exceptional new projects, and embed sustainability and inclusion even more firmly into our operations. It was also a year where we further strengthened our financial foundation, enabling continued investments and accelerated growth. 

Our performance in FY 2024-25 reflects both the strength of the real estate sector and the strategic choices we’ve made over the past several years. We ended the year with our highest-ever annual booking value of `29,444 Crores, growing 31% year-on-year on a strong base. This was supported by a 29% increase in booking volume to 25.73 Million sq. ft. Both GPL’s booking value and booking volume were the highest ever recorded by any real estate developer in India. 

Over the last three years, bookings have grown at a CAGR of 55%, with cumulative bookings of `64,203 Crores over this period. FY 2024-25 also marked the eighth consecutive year of growth in booking value for the company, reaffirming our leadership position in the Indian residential real estate sector. 

Importantly, our growth was broad-based. NCR, MMR, and Bengaluru contributed `10,523 Crores, `8,034 Crores, and `5,089 Crores respectively. Twelve different projects across Mumbai, Gurugram, Noida, Bengaluru, Pune, and Hyderabad each exceeded `1,000 Crores in booking value. No single market contributed more than 36%, and our largest project accounted for just 13%, underscoring the strength of our diversified portfolio. 

We also achieved a record `17,047 Crores in customer collections, up 49% over last year, and `7,484 Crores in operating cash flow, up by 73% over last year - both the highest ever for an Indian real estate developer. We delivered 18.4 Million sq. ft. across markets, a growth of 47%. These outcomes reflect our ability to scale responsibly while remaining deeply focused on delivery. 

On the back of this strong operating performance, we reported a 57% increase in total income to `6,848 Crores, a 65% rise in EBITDA to `1,970 Crores, and an increase of 93% in PAT to `1,400 Crores . Based on our FY 2024-25 booking performance, we expect over `7,700 Crores in EBIT and nearly `4,500 Crores in net profit to be recognised over the next 3–4 years as the projects that were sold this year are completed and achieve revenue recognition. 

This year, we also took a major step towards securing our long-term growth through a `6,000 Crores Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), the largest QIP in Indian real estate history. This reflects the strong conviction of investors in the Godrej brand and our strategic direction. The capital raised will allow us to significantly scale our project pipeline, expand into new geographies, and invest in long-term capabilities to build an even stronger, more future-ready GPL. 

Our business development strategy remained disciplined and opportunity-driven. In FY 2024-25, we added 14 new projects across Noida, Gurugram, MMR, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Pune, Ahmedabad, and Indore, with an estimated saleable area of 19 Million sq. ft. and a projected booking value of `26,450 Crores. This ensures a healthy launch pipeline and future visibility across growth markets. 

In FY 2025-26, we aim to build on this momentum and cross `32,500 Crores in residential bookings—driven by a robust set of new launches and strong sustenance sales. With a healthy balance sheet, sectoral tailwinds, and operational momentum, we are confident of maintaining our growth trajectory.

At GPL, quality is a fundamental commitment. Our dedicated 300-member quality team, reporting directly to the CEO, ensures unbiased assessments across all projects. We’ve institutionalised transparent, objective, and independent quality frameworks that set a new industry benchmark. This rigor in execution is central to the trust we have built with customers and partners alike. We recognise this is a continuous journey and are committed to ensuring quality remains on our top priority. 

We continue to evolve our customer experience journey, focusing not just on homes, but on relationships built through empathy, clarity, and consistency. Our Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 67% is a testament to this approach. From thoughtful design to responsive service, we strive to create homes that feel personal and joyful at every stage of the journey. 

# **Empowering People, Enabling Inclusion** 

We believe in empowering people—both within the company and across our value chain. Our learning academy, Alchemy, drives leadership development and capability-building at all levels. We are proud to be the first among Indian real estate companies to achieve 38.6% diversity representation, including 35.2% cis-women and 3.4% representation from LGBTQ+ individuals and persons with disabilities. 

We also digitised worker engagement, scaled mental wellness programmes, and enabled longerterm participation from construction workers— ensuring our people practices are future-ready and inclusive. 

# **Building a Greener Tomorrow** 

We recognise that our role as developers goes beyond building structures. It includes shaping sustainable, inclusive, and resilient communities. 

In FY 2024-25, we added five Net-zero Waste (Design) projects and one Net-zero Energy (Design) project to our portfolio. All our sites continue to be ISO 14001:2015 certified for Environmental Management, and sustainability targets are now embedded into senior leadership KPIs. 

Our near-term climate targets, validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), were an important milestone last year. This year, we submitted our commitment for a long-term Netzero transition to SBTi. We continue to engage vendors through joint emission reduction plans and capability-building workshops. 

**In FY 2025-26, we aim to build on this momentum and cross** `O` **32,500 Crores in residential bookings driven by a robust set of new launches and strong sustenance sales. With a healthy balance sheet, sectoral tailwinds, and operational momentum, we are confident of maintaining our growth trajectory.** 



We were included in the S&P Global 2025 Sustainability Yearbook, ranked among the top 10% of real estate companies globally, and named an Industry Mover.  We also continued to feature in the Dow Jones Emerging Markets Best in Class Index and secured a 5-star rating in GRESB for the fifth consecutive year. 

# **Meaningful Impact on Communities** 

We are proud to have fully utilised our CSR funds in FY 2024-25. Through our BOCW programmes, we reached 32,500 construction workers, unlocking `88.38 Crores in government funds. Our solid waste management efforts diverted 53,239 Tonnes from landfills and recycled 99% of construction waste at source, making GPL a Netzero waste organisation.

Through our crop residue management initiative in Punjab, we transformed 97 villages, managed 17,368 hectares of farmland, and averted over 13,800 Tonnes of CO2 emissions—driving meaningful pollution control in the process. 

The real estate sector provides tremendous long-term opportunity. Our strong balance sheet, diversified portfolio, and execution capabilities provide us the opportunity to continue to build on the momentum your business has generated over the past few years. Our ambition is not just to grow, but to do so with integrity, empathy, and purpose. 

Health and safety remain central to our approach. Our Safety Management System, built on a proactive PDCA (plan–do–check–act) cycle, is ISO 45001:2018 certified across all project sites, supporting our ‘Score Zero’ aspiration for safety incidents. 

On behalf of all of us at Godrej Properties, I would like to thank our customers, partners, investors, and shareholders for your continued support. Your belief in our journey drives us every day. 

Warm regards,

##### **44Y | M** 

## **PIROJSHA GODREJ** 

Non-Independent Director, Executive Chairperson 

Mr. Pirojsha Godrej is the Executive Chairperson of Godrej Properties, Godrej Housing Finance and a Non-Executive Director at Godrej Consumer Products and Godrej Agrovet. 

Pirojsha graduated from the Wharton School of Business in 2002, completed his Masters in International Affairs from Columbia University in 2004, and an MBA from Columbia Business School in 2008. 

Pirojsha joined GPL in 2004, became an Executive Director in 2008, and was appointed CEO of Godrej Properties in 2012. He has led the company through a phase of rapid growth. In Financial Year 2016, Godrej Properties for the first time became India's #1 publicly listed real estate developer by residential sales, a position it has retained for the past 5 years. Under Pirojsha’s leadership, Godrej Properties has been at the forefront of the sustainable development movement; in 2013, GPL received an award from former President of India, APJ Abdul Kalam for being one of the companies in India from across sectors to have driven the green building movement. 

In 2020, Godrej Properties ranked #1 amongst listed residential developers across the world in the Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmark, an organisation committed to rigorous and independent evaluation of the sustainability performance of real assets across the globe. The Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) has awarded Pirojsha the IGBC Green Champion Award 2016 for his contribution to the sustainability of India's built environment. He was also awarded with the EY Entrepreneur Of The Year™ Awards 2024: Energy, Real Estate, and Infrastructure category

##### **73Y | M** 

## **NADIR B. GODREJ** 

Non-Independent, Non-Executive Director 

Mr. Nadir B. Godrej is the Chairman and Managing Director of Godrej Industries Ltd. & Chairman of Godrej Agrovet Ltd. He has a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering from Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a Master of Science degree in Chemical Engineering from Stanford University and an MBA from Harvard Business School. 

He has been the Director of several Godrej companies since 1977 and has developed the animal feed, agricultural inputs and chemicals businesses of Godrej Industries and other associate companies, while also playing an active role in research. Mr. Godrej’s other, non-work commitments include being the President of the Alliance Francaise De Bombay, membership in and past Chairmanship of the CII National Committee on Chemicals, and previous role as an Independent Director of Indian Hotels Company Limited and Mahindra & Mahindra Limited. He is a member of the South Asia Research Centre Advisory Board of Harvard Business School. 

He has been awarded with Chevalier de Legion d’Honneur, Globoil Life Time Achievement Award – 2012, OTAI Life Time Achievement Award – 2012, Chemtec CEW Leadership & Excellence Award – 2013, Chemexcil Life Time Achievement Award – 2013, Lifetime Achievement Award by AILBIEA – 2016, CHEMTECH Leadership & Excellence Award – 2017 – Hall of Fame. 

Also, he was conferred with a Honorary Degree of Doctor of Philosophy in 2017 from the Manav Rachna University. He also received the award in Business Excellence at the IBG function in 2018 and ICC Life Time Achievement Award in 2022.  He also received a Honorary Degree in Doctor of Philosophy in Business Management from XIM University, Bhubaneshwar in 2023. Also, the Qimpro Platinum Standard 2023 Award and CLFMA Lifetime Achievement Award in 2023. He was also felicitated with ‘Green Business Titan’ Award in 2024 by the JSW The Times of India Earth Care Awards in 2024, and recently Mr. Godrej was honoured with the D.Sc. (Honoris Causa) from Institute of Chemical Technology in February 2025.

## **GAURAV 41Y | M PANDEY** 

Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer 

Mr. Gaurav Pandey brings over 20 years of real estate experience, including 8.5 years with Godrej Properties. Under his leadership, GPL achieved approximately 3.7X growth in Booking Value in three years, reaching `I` 29,444 Crores in FY 24-25, the highest annual booking value by any Indian developer for the second consecutive year. Since taking charge during FY 22-23, GPL has delivered a cumulative Booking Value of `I` 64,203 Crores, unprecedented in Indian residential real estate. GPL’s collections of `I` 17,047 Crores and operating cash flow of `I` 7,484 Crores in FY 24-25 set benchmarks for the sector. He has led over 46 transactions with a cumulative revenue potential exceeding `I` 88,500 Crores. 

Previously, as CEO of the North Zone, he strengthened financial performance, growing Booking Value by 6X, Collections by 4X, and delivering the largest contribution to GPL’s PAT. 

Before GPL, he was CEO at Burman GSC and held senior roles at PropEquity and Ascendas India. He also coanchored "The Property Show" on NDTV. 

Mr. Pandey is an Economics Honours graduate from the University of Delhi and has completed a postgraduate course from the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Kozhikode. 

He co-chairs FICCI’s Committee on Urban Development and Real Estate. He has been a CEO Council member of The Wall Street Journal since 2024 and was recognised among "The World’s Most Influential Decision Makers" by the WSJ CEO Council in 2024. 

Gaurav has been recognised as the CEO of the Year at the Construction Times BAM Awards 2025. 

He was also honoured as the Iconic Brand Leader at the Realty Plus India Brand Leadership Conclave and Awards 2025 and named one of Business World's Most Valuable CEOs. 

In addition, he was bestowed with the Pride of India award at the Construction Week Awards 2024. Under his leadership, GPL has won many accolades.

# **SUTAPA** Lead Independent Director **BANERJEE** 

Ms. Sutapa Banerjee has spent 24 years in the financial services industry across two large multinational banks (ANZ Grindlays and ABN AMRO), and a boutique Indian Investment bank (Ambit) where she built and headed several businesses and analysed multiple sectors including real estate for the money management  business. Sutapa was voted as one of the ‘Top 20 Global Rising Stars of Wealth Management’ by the Institutional Investor Group in 2007 - the only Indian and one of only two winners from Asia. As CEO she led Ambit Private Wealth to ‘Best Private Bank in India in the 2013 AsiaMoney polls. In 2012 she was shortlisted in the ‘50 most Powerful Women’ by Fortune India. 

Currently, she serves as an Independent Director on the boards of several companies and has served on the Board of Oxfam and was the Nominee Director of Women’s World Banking NY in India. She is also a visiting faculty at IIM Ahmedabad and an adjunct faculty with IICA. She works as a Decision Coach for senior leadership talent and consults in the Wealth and Investments area for the Gerson Lehrman Group. She is an Advanced Leadership Fellow (2015) at Harvard University and works as Decision Coach for senior leadership talent. 

Sutapa is a gold medalist in Economics from the XLRI school of Management in India, and an Economics major from Presidency College Kolkata. Currently she is a member of the Advisory Council of the CII Centre for Women Leadership. She has served on the CII National Committee on ‘Integrity and Transparency in Governance’, the CII National Committee on ‘Women’s Empowerment’ and the ‘Indian Women Network’.

**DR. INDU 64Y | M** Independent Director **BHUSHAN** 

Dr. Indu Bhushan has a career spanning almost 41 years across a multitude of sectors. He served for nine years in the IAS before leaving government service. After that, he worked as a Senior Economist with the World Bank Group before moving to the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in 1997. 

Dr. Bhushan holds a Ph.D. in Health Economics and a Master of Health Sciences from Johns Hopkins University. He is a B.Tech graduate from IIT BHU, holds a Post Graduate Diploma from IIT Delhi, and is also a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA). He was a member of the Indian Administrative Service (Rajasthan cadre, 1983 batch). 

He served as Director General, East Asia Department of ADB. He has held multiple positions within ADB including Director General, Strategy and Policy Department and has led ADB’s engagement with several Asian economies including the People’s Republic of China. He provided oversight to sectors like energy, environment, natural resources and agriculture, transport, public management, real estate and infrastructure, financial and regional cooperation and urban and social development. 

In 2018, Dr. Bhushan was appointed as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB - PMJAY), a flagship health assurance scheme of the Government of India covering more than 500 Million citizens. As the founding CEO, he led the design, development and the rollout of the scheme and oversaw its implementation in the country. He also initiated the implementation of the ambitious National Digital Health Mission (later renamed Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission).

### **OUTCOMES** 

## **Profit** 

Create economic value through a sustainable business model, facilitating a mutually beneficial proposition for responsible profit generation throughout our value chains. 

## **Planet** 

Minimise our environmental footprint and dependency on limited resources. Focus on maintaining water positive status as we scale, replace with "continue to work towards our 2050 Net Zero commitment". 

## **Process** 

Transform compliance into opportunities by optimising processes and allocating resources effectively. Implement robust risk assessment and management strategies, particularly to address the challenges posed by climate change. 

## **Product** 

Design and build sustainable products and services throughout our development footprint, with a comprehensive understanding of impacts generated by our products throughout their entire life cycle. 

## **People** 

Ensure the health, safety, diversity, equity, inclusion, well-being, happiness, knowledge, and care for our employees, customers, workers, and communities.

# **IN CONVERSATION WITH MD & CEO** 

### **Gaurav Pandey** 

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer 

To navigate this, we’ve doubled down on local empowerment. Our zonal leadership model allows for market-sensitive decision-making. 

## **Q. What has enabled Godrej Properties to achieve leadership in the real estate sector?** 

This is backed by professional management and data-led insights, enabling us to anticipate and act on consumer shifts quickly. 

Our leadership has been built on three core pillars: execution, discipline, and foresight. 

Between 2019 and 2021, our growth hovered around 15%. In the last two years, however, we’ve scaled rapidly, growing booking value by 56% in FY 22-23, 84% in FY 23-24, and 31% in FY 24-25 on a much higher base. This acceleration is the result of proactive capital raises at strategic junctures in FY 18-19, FY 20-21, and again in FY 24-25 with the largest QIP ever seen in the sector. 

We continue to evolve with sustainability imperatives and customer-centric design innovations. With a responsive operating model, financial discipline, and strong brand trust, we are well-equipped to lead through the next phase of change. 

Our financial agility, coupled with strong internal accruals, has allowed us to maintain a healthy balance sheet, reducing net gearing from 0.7x to ~0.2x. Equally important is our pan-India presence, which gives us operational flexibility and risk diversification across cycles. 

**We are the only developer with a truly pan India presence, which helps us balance risk while scaling efficiently. Our strategy of self-development gives us control over execution and margins critical in a sector where trust and delivery timelines matter deeply.** 

The strength of the Godrej brand continues to be a key differentiator—enabling faster partnerships, smoother market entries, and stronger customer recall. Being part of the Godrej Industries Group enhances our market position, improves access to land, and lowers our cost of capital. 



## **Q. The real estate sector is undergoing significant transformation. How is Godrej Properties navigating these changes?** 

The Indian real estate market is becoming increasingly segmented defined by varying demand drivers across regions and shifting buyer expectations. Post-COVID, we’ve seen a decisive shift: homeowners are now prioritising quality of life, larger spaces, and integrated amenities. 

## **Q. How is Godrej Properties driving sustainability across its business operations?** 

Sustainability is embedded in everything we do—from project design to operations and workforce engagement. Our inclusion in the S&P Dow Jones Best in Class Indices is a recognition of this effort, but our motivation goes beyond rankings. 

We have been successful in adding 6 IGBC Net Zero Waste (Design) and 1 IGBC Net Zero Energy (Design) project in our portfolio advancing our Net Zero commitment. 

We work closely with our supply chain to promote decarbonisation—conducting training workshops and encouraging the use of energy-efficient materials. Onsite, we focus on worker safety, upskilling, and long-term career enablement. 

We also see sustainability through the lens of inclusion. Our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) practices ensure opportunities for growth across backgrounds and roles—strengthening our social impact alongside environmental performance. 

## **Q. What initiatives has Godrej Properties undertaken to strengthen customer trust and enhance their experience?** 

Trust and experience are central to our value proposition. In FY 24-25, we reimagined home handovers into celebratory “Shubharambh” moments, with senior leadership participating to mark the occasion. This transformed handovers into a festive, deeply personal experience. 

We launched Impressions, a social media series capturing authentic stories from our customers—building relatability and advocacy. Over 200 customer videos were published, enhancing community engagement. 

Technology remains a key enabler. Our Godrej Properties mobile app (4+ rating) provides real-time purchase and project updates. The app now supports alternate payment modes and has doubled digital collections. 

Our WhatsApp-based service has also been upgraded to allow real-time audio/video support, improving responsiveness and transparency. 

These initiatives together reflect our commitment to a relationship-driven, technology-enabled, and emotionally engaging customer journey. 

## **Q. Can you provide insights into how technological innovations have enhanced operational efficiency and supported the company’s growth ambitions?** 

We’ve made significant strides in integrating technology into core functions. Our in-house design tech vertical now leverages generative AI for architectural accuracy and efficiency. By collaborating with AI startups, we’ve strengthened design delivery and minimised deviation from blueprints. 

In construction, our 3D-printed villa in Pune represents a leap forward—faster, sustainable, and highly precise. On the sales front, AI-driven analytics and personalised digital campaigns have enhanced outreach and conversion rates. 

Beyond efficiency, our innovations aim to create real impact. Our labour productivity app ensures transparent incentives and financial access, helping our workforce grow alongside us. We believe technology must uplift— not just optimise. 

## **Q. Looking ahead, what are the key priorities and strategies that will drive the next phase of growth for Godrej Properties?** 

As we move into our next phase, our priorities remain clear: scale responsibly, execute consistently, and grow profitably. 

We will deepen our presence in core regions like NCR, MMR, Pune and Bengaluru while selectively entering tier-1 and tier-2 cities with strong demand dynamics. In FY 24-25, we entered Indore through two plotted development acquisitions—reflecting our calibrated approach to market entry. 

We’re expanding across mid-income, premium, and luxury segments, and exploring lifestyle-led formats aligned with post-pandemic preferences. Sustainability will remain a core focus, with our Net Zero goals shaping design, construction, and operations. 

Disciplined capital allocation, customer centricity, and operational excellence will continue to anchor our growth strategy. We are confident that our foundation is strong— and the future is full of opportunity.

Resilience & Risk Management 

### **Risk Identification** 

### **Implementation and Validation of Management** 

We identify key sustainability and value creation factors across our ventures, operations, and initiatives, by engaging external stakeholders and assessing financial performance, climate impact, and ESG exposures. 

The Board and Senior Management review identified risks, approve outcomes, and integrate them into the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework through defined action plans. 

### **Analysing Materials and Prioritising Identified Concerns** 

### **Reporting and Monitoring** 

Risks are monitored regularly against tolerance levels. Material topics are reassessed annually with external assurance to ensure accuracy and relevance. 

We prioritise topics using the Double Materiality Principle, considering how the company affects the economy, society, and environment (Inside Out), and how external factors affect the company (Outside In). 

GPL ensures reporting consistency with a standardised definition of 'material' across all reports. Our materiality matrix integrates internal and external criteria, prioritising climate change factors to support sector goals aligned with national commitments. Acknowledging the risks and opportunities linked to climate change, we align our assessments and disclosures with globally recognised frameworks like the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosure (TCFD), CDP, and the Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi).

## **ABOUT OUR STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT PLAN** 

Understanding our stakeholders is critical to the long-term success of our business. Regular engagement with them helps to shape our strategy and ultimately informs our decisions so that we can deliver outstanding places and positive outcomes for all stakeholders. 

Our stakeholder engagement process reflects our commitment to inclusivity and transparency. We have instituted a structured approach to ensure meaningful interactions with all stakeholders, which encompasses the following key steps. 

### **STAKEHOLDER IDENTIFICATION** 

### **STAKEHOLDER PRIORITISATION** 

### **STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT PLAN** 

We identify individuals and groups who are impacted by or can impact our operations. 

We assess and rank stakeholders based on their influence, dependence, and relevance to GPL. 

We develop tailored engagement plans to address the specific needs and expectations of each stakeholder group. 

## **ENGAGING LOCAL COMMUNITY STAKEHOLDERS** 

To ensure meaningful participation, we support capacitybuilding initiatives that help local stakeholders effectively engage with the company. 

We conduct Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) at all project sites to evaluate potential effects on surrounding communities and ecosystems. These include localised stakeholder impact assessments to identify specific social, economic, and environmental concerns, forming the basis for targeted mitigation plans. 

We regularly conduct perception surveys and community reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of our engagement strategies and identify emerging issues. These are supplemented by direct meetings with community representatives to ensure concerns are promptly addressed. 

To foster transparency and trust, we have established clear and accessible communication channels with local stakeholders. These include structured community meetings, consultations, surveys, CSR initiatives, and awareness Programmes. Project-related information is shared proactively in a clear, timely, and culturally appropriate manner. 

All grievances are tracked through a formal mechanism that ensures timely resolution and continuous improvement. Our stakeholder engagement Programmes are applied consistently across all local operations, reinforcing our commitment to inclusive, responsible, and responsive development. 

We actively encourage feedback through multiple contact points—such as email, helplines, and inperson interactions—outlined in our publicly available Stakeholder Engagement Policy.

## **GPL COMMITTEES** 

Our Corporate Governance framework is designed to foster sustainable and transparent growth, while consistently generating economic value and safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders. We champion fair and transparent business practices through a well-structured corporate governance framework that not only guides ethical decisionmaking but also ensures active and inclusive engagement with all stakeholders. 

Eight board-led committees provide strategic oversight across critical focus areas, shaping corporate direction, ensuring effective implementation, and monitoring performance, risk, and policy adherence. The Board of Directors recognises that diversity is integral to long-term success, and currently comprises seven members with varied geographic origins, age groups, genders, ethnicities, cultural backgrounds, professional skills, and industry expertise, enhancing GPL’s agility and competitiveness. 

The Board of Directors plays a central role in ensuring effective governance, overseeing the implementation of strategic decisions, and maintaining a culture of accountability across the organisation. By prioritising fairness in our interactions with regulators, employees, customers, vendors, investors, and the broader community, we reinforce our commitment to responsible corporate citizenship. 

During the financial year, the Board met four times, following a structured and outcome-oriented agenda. We remain committed to maintaining at least 50% independent representation on the Board and enforce a minimum 50% attendance requirement for all board members to uphold accountability and effective governance. 

As a publicly listed entity, GPL rigorously complies with the corporate governance norms prescribed by the National Stock Exchange of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), including the appointment of independent directors to its Board, further strengthening our dedication to oversight, transparency, and stakeholder trust.

# **ESG GOVERNANCE** 

ESG governance is anchored in a multi-tiered structure that ensures strategic oversight, operational accountability, and organisation-wide engagement. At the apex sits the Board-level ESG Steering Committee, which provides high-level direction and oversight on sustainability priorities, social issues and climate risks. 

Reporting into this Board Committee is the Executive ESG Committee, chaired by the Chief Design and Sustainability Officer. This crossfunctional committee drives the integration of ESG goals, such as climate risk management, social equity, and ethical governance, into business strategy and operations. 

The Executive Committee is supported by specialised ESG team lead by the ESG head focused on areas like Climate Action, ESG Reporting, Human Rights, and Employee Engagement. ESG performance is regularly reviewed through structured reporting cycles, with ESG-linked KPIs embedded into leadership performance evaluations and incentives, covering themes such as energy efficiency, health & safety, talent development, and stakeholder satisfaction. 

This tiered model enables cross-functional collaboration, aligns ESG priorities with business objectives, and reinforces GPL’s commitment to transparent, responsible, and sustainable growth. 

We have a robust process to identify, assess, address and report transparently on actual and potential human rights risks across our business and enable us to remediate any adverse impact it has or could cause. We acknowledge that human rights due diligence is an ongoing process, requiring particular attention during critical phases of our business operations. As a result, we regularly review the risk mapping of potential issues, adjust our processes and integrate the requirements with our policies. We are committed to remedying any impact on human rights during our business operations. 

We conducted Human Rights Self-Assessment (HRSA) across all active project sites (including own operations, contractors and joint ventures) in reporting boundary and GPL offices, following GPL’s Human Rights Policy and the guidelines set forth by the United Nations on Human Rights. External third-party audits were undertaken across 6 sites on our internal human rights processes 

and no instances of noncompliance were found across our sites, thereby obviating the necessity for remedial actions. However, minor observations were noted and were addressed. 

# **FREEDOM OF ASSOCIATION** 

We fully respect and uphold the right to freedom of association as a fundamental human right to our employees and workers. We recognise our employees’ right to form, join, or refrain from joining trade unions or other lawful associations of their choosing, in accordance with applicable laws and international labour standards. We are committed to ensuring that all employees can exercise this right without fear of discrimination, retaliation, or interference. However, there are no employees involved in any trade unions or other associations. 

# **HUMAN RIGHTS: CHAMPIONING EQUALITY** 

We uphold human rights as a fundamental principle, embedding it across our operations, workforce, independent contractors, supply chain, and stakeholder engagements. Our commitment policies align with global frameworks, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the International Labour Organisation’s Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, as well as United Nations human rights guidelines. Our Human Rights policy applies to our operations and the entities in which we own a majority interest. We are dedicated to ensuring that all rightsholders, including our employees, contract workers, suppliers, communities around our operations, consumers, and customers, are well informed about our commitment and know how to report any violations. We also have a Supplier Code of Conduct that outlines the ethical and responsible business practices for our suppliers. 

We prohibit the employment of individuals under the age of 18 years. We forbid the use of all forms of force in the workplace. 

Further we prohibit child, adolescent, bonded or compulsory labour, including any form of human trafficking. 

Through rigorous due diligence, we assess and mitigate human rights risks across our value chain, extending protections to employees, contractual workers, construction labourers, and supply chain partners. 

We have implemented mandatory training on critical human rights aspects, such as Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) and antidiscrimination policies, reinforcing our commitment to ethical workplace practices. 

We assess and identify actual and potential human rights impacts by regularly organising systematic human rights risk assessments covering our own operations, value chain and business relations like joint venture entities in which we own a majority interest.  In addition to our own employees and contract workers, the due diligence process covers vulnerable groups and focusses on individuals and groups who are at higher risk due to their vulnerability or marginalisation. This includes migrant workers, children, women, sexual and gender minorities, ethnic and racial groups, persons with disability and indigenous people. The human right assessment covers various human rights issues which include: 

- Child labour 

- Working hours, wages and leaves 

- Forced labour 

- Fair treatment and equal remuneration 

- Discrimination 

- Community impact 

- Freedom of Association 

- Collective bargaining 

- Health and Safety 

# **CORPORATE CODE OF POLICIES** 

To maintain compliance with legal and ethical standards, we have implemented a set of corporate codes and policies as listed below. All codes and policies are approved by the board of the directors and reviewed regularly to ensure alignment with widely accepted industry standards. 

# **CODE OF CONDUCT** 

Ethical conduct is fundamental to our 

organisation's success. Our Code of Conduct (CoC) acts as a guide, directing every employee, board member, and senior leader toward principled behaviour. The Code governs: Vendor/Suppliers , Practices and Procedures for Fair, Disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information , Board of Directors and Senior Management and Employees. 

## **Reporting of Breach of Code of Conduct** 

All employees, irrespective of their employment status (full-time, part-time, or daily wage) or role (permanent, temporary, ad hoc, consultant, probationary, trainee, or intern), are responsible for promptly reporting any breach, whether direct or indirect, of the Code of Conduct (CoC). 

This report should be made to their manager, Business Head, HR department, or designated whistleblowing officer. 

### Consequences of Violations 

Any individual found to have violated the CoC or engaged in fraudulent activities will be subject to immediate termination from the organisation. 

In such instances, a First Information Report (FIR) will be filed at the local police station, and necessary steps will be taken to recover the fraudulent amount. 

The names of individuals involved in fraudulent activities will be communicated internally through official channels, informing all employees of their termination. 

Furthermore, the name(s) of the individual(s) will be publicly disclosed in local newspapers to notify external stakeholders of our disassociation with them. Details will be shared as deemed necessary.

# **COMPLIANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM** 

We place strong emphasis on legal and regulatory compliance as a cornerstone of responsible and ethical business conduct. To support this, we leverage Legatrix, an advanced IT-enabled legal compliance platform that equips our management with a centralised dashboard for real-time visibility into the company’s compliance landscape. 

# **ANTI-CORRUPTION** 

We recognise that corruption, including bribery in all forms poses significant risks with potentially severe consequences for our business and stakeholders. Our Code of Conduct comprehensively outlines our approach to anti-bribery and anti-corruption, serving as a central guide for all employees, directors, and third-party partners. To proactively address this, we have established a comprehensive Anti-Corruption Compliance Programme, which serves as a robust framework to prevent, detect, and respond to compliance-related concerns. This programme is a key component of our broader strategy to combat financial crimes and uphold ethical standards. 

This platform enhances governance by issuing timely reminders, tracking post-filing documentation, mapping applicable regulatory requirements, and maintaining a secure repository for compliance-related records. Our commitment extends to social and economic compliance, with no reported instances of non-compliance related to these parameters during the reporting period. 

To ensure the effectiveness and integrity of our compliance framework, it is regularly audited by our Assurance Partner, reinforcing our dedication to transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement. 

It explicitly prohibits offering, accepting, or soliciting bribes or improper advantages, whether through gifts, services, cash equivalents, discounts, loans, or any other item of value that could unduly influence business decisions. We strictly govern political contributions, charitable donations, and sponsorships to prevent their misuse as indirect forms of bribery. These activities are permitted only under defined policies and are subject to transparency, disclosure, and review to ensure full compliance with legal and ethical norms. 

# **ETHICS AND COMPLIANCE** 

We believe that embedding ethical conduct across all levels of the organisation is essential for effective operations, risk mitigation, and long-term value creation. A strong ethical foundation enhances our reputation, builds customer and employee loyalty, and strengthens investor confidence. 

We uphold a culture of integrity, accountability, and transparency through a comprehensive set of governance and ethics policies that guide behaviour across the business. ## **WHISTLEBLOWER MECHANISM** 

- The whistleblower platform is managed independently by a third party 

The Whistleblowing mechanism provides a platform where instances of code breaches, discrimination, harassment, or safety concerns can be reported anonymously. During the quarterly meetings of the Audit Committee, the Board of Directors is informed of every complaint. 

- The whistleblowing platform allows for anonymous submission of complaints. All complaints and identities of whistleblowers are handled with the utmost confidentiality, in accordance with the wishes of the complainant. 

A robust whistleblower mechanism is a cornerstone of ethical and transparent governance within any organisation. It fosters a culture of accountability and integrity by providing employees, stakeholders, and other parties with a secure and trustworthy avenue to report any unethical, illegal, or unsafe behaviour. The salient features of our whistleblowing mechanism are highlighted below: 

   - The whistleblower policy has a strict zero-tolerance policy against any form of retaliation towards whistleblowers. Any form of discharge, threat, discrimination, or other adverse action against a whistleblower is strictly prohibited. 

   - To ensure effective utilisation of the whistleblower mechanism, regular training Programmes are conducted for all employees. These sessions cover the purpose of the mechanism, how to access the reporting platform, and the protections afforded to whistleblowers. 

- We have a dedicated Whistleblower Officer for managing whistleblower complaints. 

- The whistleblowing mechanism provides a platform where instances of code violations, discrimination, harassment, or safety concerns can be reported. 

   - The process for investigating reports is clearly defined within the whistleblower policy. Each report is assessed promptly, and investigations are carried out in an unbiased and systematic manner. Findings are documented, and appropriate corrective actions are taken based on the outcomes of each investigation. 

- There are four ways of reaching out to the whistle blowing platform: telephone, Email, Web Portal and Chat bot.

## **RISK GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE** 

# **ANTICIPATING TOMORROW'S CHALLENGES** 

We are cognisant that risks represent potential events or circumstances that could impact our operations, financial performance, reputation, or stakeholders. The objective of our risk management is to establish a risk-aware and risk-intelligent culture that supports decision-making and helps improve performance. 

## **WHERE RISKS ARISE** 

**The risk classification at GPL categorises risk into 4 categories based on the source where it stems from:** 

#### **Operational Challenges** 

#### **External Environment Risks** 

These risks arise from the day-to-day execution of construction and project management activities, including site safety, contractor performance, supply chain disruptions, quality control, and adherence to timelines and regulatory requirements. Prompt risk management is vital for seamless operations. 

These arise from economic, market, geopolitical, or regulatory changes beyond our control. We prioritise identifying, analysing, and evaluating these risks for effective management. 

#### **Sustainability Concerns** 

#### **Financial Volatility** 

These relate to financial activities and reporting, like liquidity, interest rates, and credit. Active monitoring and management are crucial for financial stability. 

These cover ESG factors impacting operations and reputation. This includes factors such as climate risks, rising temperature, biodiversity loss, employee welfare, and community involvement. Integrating sustainability into risk management fosters responsible business practices. 

We have implemented a strong and structured risk governance framework to ensure that potential risks are systematically identified, evaluated, and managed. 

### **Board Level Oversight** 

Our Board has the overarching responsibility for the governance of risk management, including its strategic alignment and effective implementation, with support from the Risk committee. Our Risk Committee, at the board level, comprises of Independent Directors. We have adopted the three lines of defence model as a framework for risk governance. This model is structured to mitigate conflicts of interest and to uphold independent oversight of risk management activities.

# **RISK MANAGEMENT APPROACH** 

We follow a proactive and structured approach to risk management, embedding it deeply within our strategic and annual business planning cycles. This ensures that risk oversight evolves in tandem with our business priorities and external landscape. 

# **RISK MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES** 

The objective of risk management at GPL is to establish a risk aware and risk-intelligent culture that supports decision-making and helps improve performance. An effective risk management framework requires consistent processes for assessment, risk response, monitoring and communication of risk issues across the Company. The ERM Manual provides a structured and disciplined approach to the risk management process to facilitate informed 

decision-making on risks, with specific objectives mentioned below: 

### **Identify Risks**

# **RISK APPETITE** 

Risk appetite forms a foundational part of our risk management approach. It defines the level and type of risk we are willing to accept in pursuit of our strategic and operational objectives. For each identified risk, we assess its potential impact and likelihood, and evaluate it against our predefined appetite thresholds, ranging from zero to high tolerance.  Risk appetite levels are determined in alignment with business goals and are embedded into the annual risk assessment cycle, guiding the development of mitigation plans and influencing the review process by the Risk Management Committees. By integrating risk appetite into our governance framework, we ensure a balanced approach, encouraging innovation and growth while safeguarding organisational resilience.

The risk assessment function is structurally independent of business and is overseen and coordinated by the central corporate audit function. The risk assessment outcomes fall under the ownership of the respective business function heads. This collaborative approach ensures a comprehensive and efficient risk management strategy across the organisation.

- We provide regular risk management education for all nonexecutive directors. 

- We use multiple channels and formats to raise awareness about key risks, distributing communication products via email and workplace platforms. 

- We provide information on cyber risks, data privacy, and compliance with regulations. 

## **Training** 

- We conduct focused training on risk management principles throughout the organisation. 

- We organise workshops for key functions, such as general managers and to improve their understanding of risk-related issues. New managers are inducted on Enterprise Risk Management training. They are trained on inputs on risk definition, identification, rating, classification, prioritisation, mitigation, control, and review. 

## **Drills and Tests** 

- We conduct periodic crisis management drills to simulate scenarios like fires, sabotage incidents, and falls from height. 

- We test business continuity plans, including information security, at least once a year. 

## **New product Development** 

Risk is embedded in the new product development process through structured assessments at key milestones, such as concept validation, design, and go-to-market planning. Cross-functional teams evaluate potential risks related to market demand, regulatory compliance, supply chain, and execution feasibility. 

## **Performance Metrics/ Incentives** 

Based on the nature of risks—such as operational, financial, or sustainability, etc.—employee performance metrics for the relevant business functions are defined, including associated financial incentive. 

## **Stakeholder Communication** 

- We engage with stakeholders through comprehensive reports to communicate key risks, risk management measures, controls in place, and emerging risks. 

- We ensure stakeholders understand our risk landscape and mitigation efforts.

# **CHAMPIONING CLIMATE POLICY THROUGH ADVOCACY** 

Our approach to public policy engagement and climate advocacy is grounded in our commitment to sustainability and responsible corporate citizenship. Recognising the far-reaching implications of climate change for our business and communities, we actively support policies aligned with the Paris Agreement and a just transition to a low-carbon economy. 

To ensure our lobbying efforts and trade association memberships reflect these objectives, we have instituted a structured, transparent governance framework that holds us accountable to both our climate goals and our stakeholders: 

## **EXECUTIVE OVERSIGHT** 

Our public policy engagements are governed through a clearly defined framework with accountabilities extending to the relevant functional senior executive levels. The Managing Director & CEO plays a pivotal leadership role, including co-chairing the FICCI Committee on Urban Development and Real Estate, reinforcing our commitment at the strategic level. 

## **POLICY POSITION STATEMENT** 

We have publicly articulated our support for the goals of the Paris Agreement, including limiting global warming to well below 2°C and pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. This position informs all our advocacy and policy engagement efforts. 

## **MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS** 

A centralised and robust management system is in place to oversee lobbying activities and trade association memberships. This system includes detailed documentation of our engagements, representatives, financial contributions, and alignment with business and sustainability objectives. 

## **MONITORING, REVIEW, AND ALIGNMENT PROCESSES** 

Our approach ensures transparency, consistency, and alignment with international climate goals through the following mechanisms: 

### **Direct Lobbying Activities** 

All climate-related lobbying initiatives are reviewed regularly to ensure consistency with our climate strategy and the principles of the Paris Agreement. These activities are documented, monitored for effectiveness, and subject to internal oversight. 

### **Trade Associations** 

We maintain a centralised database of all trade association memberships. This database includes information such as the purpose of the association, our representatives, membership costs, and the strategic value derived from participation. Regular reviews are conducted to evaluate continued alignment with our climate and business goals. 

### **Misalignment Assessment and Response** 

We have established a clear framework to assess and address potential misalignments between the climate-related positions of trade associations and our own. Where discrepancies are identified, we engage constructively with the association to encourage alignment or consider withdrawing from the membership if alignment cannot be achieved. 

#### **Functional Oversight and Audit** 

Senior functional leaders are responsible for overseeing trade association memberships within their departments to ensure relevance and alignment with strategic objectives. In addition, our Internal Audit team conducts 

periodic reviews to verify compliance with internal policies and external regulatory requirements, ensuring transparency and ethical conduct. 

## **TRANSPARENCY AND REPORTING** 

We are committed to transparent disclosure of our climate advocacy efforts. Our reporting includes details of our direct climate-related lobbying activities and positions and climate-related initiatives of the trade associations we are part of. We also continuously review how these engagements align with our climate policy. 

## **GLOBAL COVERAGE AND PARTNERSHIPS** 

Our policy advocacy and engagement efforts towards climate policy support are consistent across all our operations. Our strategic partnerships with organisations such as the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD) and FICCI are leveraged to promote collective action, industry innovation, and policy advancement toward a net-zero future. 

We affirm that we have made no financial contributions to any political party in FY 2024–25. We are members of the following affiliations with trade and industry chambers/ associations: 

- Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) 

- Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) 

- World Bank Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD)

# **NAVIGATING CLIMATE REALITIES** 

We recognise that the influence of climate change extends beyond our immediate operational sites, permeating our entire value chain. We are dedicated to building climate resilience and have incorporated the TCFD’s guidance since 2021 to approach the risks posed by the changing climate on the business. 

## **ESG & CLIMATE RISK GOVERNANCE** 

To drive accountability, ESG performance metrics are embedded within our annual objectives, with executive compensation directly linked to achieving critical sustainability targets. We continue to integrate climate risk mitigation into our procurement processes, operations, and project transitions, ensuring a structured and effective approach to sustainability. 

At the management level, we have taken key initiatives to drive accountability and align ESG with financial performance: 

- Sustainability targets are now embedded within annual objectives, with corresponding compensation structures tied to their achievement across all roles, departments, and business functions. 

- Executive remuneration is directly linked to the successful delivery of key performance indicators (KPIs) related to material sustainability challenges, reinforcing leadership accountability in driving ESG progress. We have identified KPIs (both financial and non-financial) around each level and we monitor the achievement of the same annually.

## **HOW WE GOVERN CLIMATE-RELATED RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES** 

### **Board-Level ESG Committee** 

Provides strategic oversight on ESG and climate-related issues. Defines sustainability goals, shapes investor communications, monitors progress on key indicators and evaluates interventions. Climate issues are integrated into the Board’s agenda and reviewed annually. 

### **Zonal CEOs and Operational Leadership** 

Oversees execution of ESG and climate plans at the zonal level. Ensures timely and accurate ESG data reporting, conducts quarterly compliance reviews, maintains EMS audit readiness, ensures worker registration under BOCW, and manages R&D and capital investments in sustainable construction technologies. 

### **Chief Design and Sustainability Officer (CDSO)** 

Leads the formulation of sustainability strategy and implementation plans. Coordinates with zonal teams and monitors enterprise-wide progress towards ESG objectives. 

### **Project Directors and Environmental Managers** 

Implements ESG plans at the project site level. Ensures accurate and timely data reporting, addresses data discrepancies, explains significant variances, and enforces ISO 14001 EMS protocols with a focus on achieving zero non-conformities. 

### **Climate Risk Recognition and Context** 

We acknowledge climaterelated risks as a material consideration for our business, particularly given the real estate sector’s significant contribution to global emissions. In light of increasing global momentum towards decarbonisation, netzero targets, and international frameworks such as the Paris Agreement, we are actively assessing physical climate risks—including storms, floods, and extreme heat, changing weather patterns—to embed resilience and longterm sustainability into our strategic planning. 

### **Internal Integration of ESG and Financial Alignment** 

To align our financial strategy with sustainability goals, we have fully embedded ESG considerations into core business operations. ESG performance is now integrated into annual targets, procurement protocols, and executive remuneration frameworks, reinforcing our commitment to longterm value creation through responsible and climateconscious decision-making. 

### **External Dependencies and Regulatory Influence** 

Progress towards netzero targets depends not only on internal action but also on strong regulatory frameworks and collaborative partnerships. Recognising that a substantial share of our emissions lies beyond our direct operational control, we view government policies, industry standards, and evolving climate mandates as critical enablers in advancing our decarbonisation efforts.

### **Transition Risk** 

We identify transition risks under both the Below 2°C and Net Zero Emissions (NZE) scenarios (orderly transition scenarios). While physical risks are relatively subdued in these pathways, transition risks are elevated due to stringent policies and rising stakeholder expectations. 

In contrast, under a “business-as-usual” scenario, delayed climate action may keep transition risks low in the short term but significantly heightens physical risks, potentially causing severe disruptions. 

The identified risks span reputational, regulatory, technological, and market-related categories. These have been classified based on their potential severity, ranging from low to high-medium risk, with corresponding opportunities also recognised.

As GPL continues to expand its projects, we remain focused on assessing and addressing climate vulnerabilities across geographies. # **Managing Transition Risks Through Strategic Climate Action** 

As part of our climate strategy and in line with our commitment to mitigate transition risks associated with the shift to a low-carbon economy, we have established a structured Internal Carbon Pricing (ICP) mechanism. 

GHG emissions: Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (indirect from purchased energy), and Scope 3 (value chain emissions). The ICP plays a critical role in reshaping our supply chain and material sourcing strategy. 

This is a strategic tool designed to align capital allocation, procurement, and operational decisions with our longterm Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi)-validated decarbonisation goals. 

## **Current ICP Structure** 

We have implemented an implicit pricing model with a preliminary internal carbon price of `978 per metric tonne of CO2e, designed to assess and influence the emissions intensity of investment and procurement decisions without immediate cash flow implications. 

Following the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) recommendations and aligned with CDP's ICP objectives, our ICP accounts for all scopes of 

## **Strategic Objectives of Implementing Internal Carbon Pricing** 

Our ICP is designed to support multiple cross-functional climate and business objectives: 

- Conduct cost-benefit analysis of low-carbon alternatives and technologies 

   - Navigate evolving carbon regulations and markets, including India’s upcoming domestic carbon market under the 2022 Energy Conservation Bill 

- Drive energy efficiency in design, construction, and operations 

   - Reduce upstream emissions through climatealigned sourcing and supplier Programmes 

- Incentivise low-carbon investments across the project lifecycle 

   - Achieve climate targets and policies, including our SBTi-validated Scope 3 goals 

- Embed climate-related considerations in business and investment decision-making 

   - Set a carbon offset budget for unavoidable emissions 

- Strengthen climate risk assessments by incorporating emissions costs into project planning 

   - Stress-test investments for carbon price resilience and long-term sustainability 

- Identify and capitalise on low-carbon opportunities, such as material innovation and green building certifications 

   - Supplier engagement strategies, aligned with our SBTi commitment 

- Inform and influence strategic and financial planning by integrating climate costs into budgeting 

- Meet Stakeholder Expectations by demonstrating transparent and responsible climate action 

## **How we Measure our Progress** 

Our climate-related goals are deeply integrated with our broader Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) commitments, which are embedded across all levels of the organisation— from leadership to operational teams. 

To monitor our progress, we utilise comprehensive internal dashboards and ensure transparent public reporting, supported by third-party assurance. 

As part of our commitment to sustainability, we have implemented a company-wide Occupational Health & Safety (OH&S) Management System and an Environmental Management System (EMS). The attainment of ISO certifications across our construction sites further reflects our dedication to climate resilience and environmental stewardship. 

Godrej Properties operates as a water-positive and carbon-neutral organisation for Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. We remain focused on reducing emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 categories, while actively working to minimise waste generation throughout our operations. 

To measure our progress against the commitments for climate risk management, we have set targets across decarbonisation (scope emission intensities), waste, water and certification of our green buildings. 

**Read more about Environment Target and Progress at Pg. 44** 

## **Our Climate Commitments** 

During the 2023-2024 fiscal year, we carried out a comprehensive risk assessment and scenario analysis pertaining to climate change, aligning with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climaterelated Financial Disclosures (TCFD) Framework. Throughout this reporting period, we have prioritised the management of climate changerelated risks. 

In accordance with the Paris Agreement, we have been active participants in the Science Based Target (SBT) initiative since 2020. Our approved targets seek to achieve a 72.6% reduction in scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions per square metre by the 2035 fiscal year. 

Moving forward, we remain steadfast in our commitment to evaluating the financial implications of climate change on our business operations. During the upcoming Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) reporting cycle, we are committed to disclosing quantified impacts, encompassing both risks and opportunities, across a range of climate change scenarios. Furthermore, our enterprise risk management framework will systematically incorporate real-world climate change risks. 

# **THE ROAD AHEAD** 

Our Internal Carbon Price is a dynamic tool that will continuously adapt to our sustainability roadmap, market developments, and regulatory shifts. By internalising the cost of carbon, we aim to drive systemic behaviouralthe resilience of our real estate portfolio in a rapidly transitioning global economy.

# **UNITED FOR A LOW-CARBON FUTURE** 

## **Managing Crop Residue** 

Changing weather patterns have significantly disrupted cropping cycles, leading farmers in North India to resort to stubble burning due to delayed monsoons. This practice contributes substantially to air pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR). 

Our Crop Residue Management (CRM) initiative aligns with the 2020 guidelines for CRM in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and the National Capital Territory of Delhi, as outlined by the Indian government. In FY 2024-25, 17,368 hectares of farmland were saved from stubble burning across 97 villages - an impressive increase from 4,966 hectares the year before. The harvested stubble was creatively reused: converted into biomass pellets, applied as soil mulch, and used as fuel in sugarcane processing plants. A notable shift began in FY 24-25 with 

the launch of the “Jalana Nahin, Galana Hai” initiative, promoting composting over burning. 

This marks a major stride toward environmental sustainability and improved soil health. With continued commitment, skill development, and collaborative efforts, this forward-thinking strategy could redefine how paddy stubble is viewed and handled, transforming a persistent problem into a sustainable development opportunity. Also, to scale up this initiative, Godrej properties in collaboration with Feedback Foundation and with the support of the Agriculture Department, are establishing a Crop Residue Management Park at Village Bhagwanpur, Gurdaspur. Spanning 10 acres, this park will serve as a demonstration and learning site for composting practices using paddy stubble. 

## **Planting Seeds of Change** 

In our pursuit of carbon neutrality, we have launched 'Afforestation of Land' programmes across India. Collaborating with Nisarg, we implemented SALM project on farmlands and ensured 95% survival rate of plants planted in community land in Beed in previous FYs. The SALM and tree plantation project has sequestered approximately 47,948.8 tCO2e through integrated climate-smart interventions. Key activities included improved crop varieties, kitchen gardens, biogas units, summer ploughing, mango agro-horticulture, and fodder cultivation. These practices enhanced soil carbon, biomass productivity, and long-term ecosystem sustainability.

###### **Organic Waste** 

Hazardous waste includes materials like solvents, cleaning agents, lead-based paints and oils, which can pose risks to human health, the environment, or property. Metal scrap is processed through certified recyclers, while construction debris is routed to municipality-authorised agencies in full compliance with regulations.

# **REPLENISH AND REUSE: WATER FOR THE LONG RUN** 

Climate change is steadily impacting groundwater availability for everyday use. To address this growing concern, we are adopting climate-resilient water management solutions within our communities. One such initiative is the development of water retention ponds - engineered to capture and store rainwater while preserving the site's natural contours. Through such thoughtful design, we are creating communities that are better equipped to manage water sustainably and live in greater harmony with nature. 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
Water Retention pond at Godrej City<br><!-- End of picture text -->

# **FROM DRYLANDS TO LIFELINES** 

Water scarcity remains one of the most urgent challenges of our time. We recognised the need for proactive, community-focused solutions and launched an integrated watershed development project in 2016. Spanning approximately 3,300 hectares, the initiative covered the villages of Bavi, Zapewadi, and Jamb in Maharashtra’s drought-prone Beed district. 

The implementation phase was successfully completed in 2019, made possible through the invaluable support of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and our NGO partner. To assess the real, on-ground impact of the intervention, we collaborated with the Ekonnect Knowledge Foundation for an independent evaluation. 

# **POND REJUVENATION AT GODREJ SUNRISE ESTATE, CHENNAI** 

We undertook the transformation of a long-neglected pond into a thriving rainwater harvesting system. This initiative went beyond infrastructure; it revitalised a forgotten space to serve both environmental and community needs. 

An advanced stormwater drainage network was installed to capture and reuse rainwater, helping mitigate flood risk and support groundwater recharge. Around the rejuvenated pond, we developed a tranquil community park that offers green open spaces for recreation and wellness. Thoughtfully integrated landscaping and water features further reduced the urban heat island effect, creating a more pleasant and sustainable microclimate for residents. 

**WE HAVE BEEN ABLE TO GIVE BACK (25X) MORE THAN WE CONSUMED DURING OUR OPERATIONS, THUS BECOMING WATER POSITIVE** 

## **Harnessing Natural Topography for Sustainable Water Management** 

At Godrej City in Panvel, Maharashtra, we have utilised the site's natural topography to develop a sustainable and efficient water management system. With an average monsoon rainfall of around 450 mm per month, we constructed a strategically located water retention pond at an intermediate elevation, aligning with the natural contours and slopes of the land. Covering a catchment area of approximately 22 acres, the pond captures and stores rainwater, which is then distributed downstream using gravity flow. 

Designed to hold up to 4 Million litres of water, the retention pond is lined with a durable HDPE geomembrane. Weep holes on the upstream side allow gradual percolation into a separate storage tank, helping extend water availability into the post-monsoon months of September and October. This system significantly reduces dependence on external water sources such as tankers, thereby promoting sustainability and improving operational efficiency.

# **BIODIVERSITY RISK ASSESSMENTS** 

We prioritise the identification and monitoring of protected areas surrounding our project sites to evaluate and minimise our impact on them. We recognise biodiversity as a critical component of sustainable development. Our Biodiversity Risk Assessment Process is designed to systematically identify, evaluate, and manage nature-related risks across our operations and value chain. 

We follow a structured, location-specific approach to assess biodiversity risks, focusing on how our own operations, adjacent areas and value chain interact with nature. This means assessing dependencies (e.g., water regulation, flood protection, air purification) and impacts (e.g., habitat disruption, pollution, land use change) at specific project sites and along the upstream and downstream segments of our operations. 

Our biodiversity risk assessment process is guided by globally recognised methodologies and frameworks like the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) LEAP approach, to ensure consistency, reliability, and transparency in identifying and managing naturerelated risks. 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
Tree plantation at Godrej Hillview Estate<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## **Biodiversity Risk Assessment Process** 

### **DEFINE SCOPE** 

Identify project sites, adjacent areas (within 5-10 km), and relevant upstream/ downstream activities. 

### **IDENTIFY DEPENDENCIES AND IMPACTS** 

Assess how operations rely on and affect natural ecosystems (e.g., water use, habitat disruption). 

### **SCREEN SENSITIVE AREAS** 

Use tools like IBAT, WWF Risk Filter, and ENCORE to map biodiversity risks at specific locations. - to be checked. 

### **CLASSIFY RISKS** 

Categorise risks as physical, regulatory, reputational, or operational and integrated in the the organisation risk management framework. 

### **CONSULT STAKEHOLDERS** 

Engage local communities, biodiversity experts, and regulators for validation and input. 

### **INTEGRATE AND ACT** 

Feed results into risk management; prepare mitigation plans and implement site-level actions. 

### **MONITOR AND REPORT** 

Track biodiversity KPIs, apply mitigation hierarchy, and disclose performance. 

# **RESTORING WHILE WE BUILD** 

A structured mitigation approach is followed, emphasising avoidance, minimisation, restoration, and offsetting to reduce environmental impact. 

Environmental Impact Assessments are undertaken at every site in accordance with Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change (MoEFCC) regulations. 

In FY 24-25, we carried out comprehensive biodiversity surveys at Maanhinjewadi in Pune, Sumthana in Nagpur, Sector 49 in Gurgaon, Banerghatta and Whitefield in Bengaluru to gain deeper insights into the local ecosystem, including flora, fauna, and ecological dynamics. Specialised stream surveys were conducted to document native topography, enabling us to align our development activities with the goal of minimising habitat disturbance. The primary biodiversity risks identified from the above assessments include habitat degradation and vegetation loss from land-use changes, soil degradation and erosion due to construction, air pollution, elevated noise levels; and introduction of invasive species threatening native biodiversity. We have devised comprehensive mitigation measures such as afforestation, native species restoration, pollution control, rainwater harvesting, installation of sewage treatment plants, and creating green buffers to safeguard local ecosystems. These surveys are being extended to all our development sites. 

We refrain  from operational activities in notified areas, eco-sensitive zones, World Heritage sites, and IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) Category I-IV protected areas. 

We have taken meaningful steps toward achieving a net positive impact on biodiversity by going beyond mitigation to ensuring that the natural environment is left in a better state than before development. Our projects are designed to integrate sustainable amenities, including rainwater harvesting systems, solar panels, and other ecofriendly initiatives that actively reduce carbon emissions while promoting a healthier living environment. We are committed to conserving 15% to 20% of the natural topography across all developments. This year, we strengthened our biodiversity efforts by planting 6,227 trees across operational regions. 

We are committed to achieving a net positive impact (NPI) on biodiversity by 2035 and “No Net Deforestation” by 2030 across all operations. 

## **Our Structured Approach to Mitigating Environmental Impact** 

### **1. AVOIDANCE** 

### **4. OFFSETTING** 

- Operations, construction, and development activities are strictly prohibited in legally protected areas, including IUCN-designated categories Ia, Ib, II, III, and IV. 

   - Initiatives include enhancing vegetation on barren lands and establishing medicinal plantations in community spaces, with active engagement of local communities. 

      - Planting native species is prioritised to foster ecological restoration. 

- Technical standards have been established to incorporate biodiversity and ecosystem management into decisionmaking processes for both new and existing projects. 

   - 

- Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are implemented to prevent the introduction of invasive species during transportation of vehicles and goods. 

### **2. MINIMISATION** 

### **5. TRANSFORMATION** 

- Environmental Management Plans (EMPs) are employed to mitigate air, noise, water, and soil pollution. 

   - Conservation activities include protecting endangered species, setting up conservation centres, offering wildlife rescue services, and supporting forest fire prevention measures. 

- Greenbelt development initiatives are undertaken to reduce the impact of pollutants. 

   - Local community involvement is promoted through livelihood improvement initiatives, public awareness campaigns, and training for forest personnel. 

- Compliance with Biodiversity Management Plans is regularly reviewed across all project sites. 

- Sustainable practices are encouraged through the use of eco-certified wood. 

### **3. RESTORATION** 

- Restoration efforts focus on replanting native and endangered flora, removing invasive species, rehabilitating disturbed areas, and restoring water bodies to conserve biodiversity.
